## Module 0 Question 1
# Data Cleaning and EDA
Task: Predicting student comfort with statistics using class experience
Response: stat.comf
Predictors: courses (PSTAT 115, PSTAT 160, PSTAT 171, PSTAT 175)

```{r}
# load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(tidymodels)
library(fastDummies)
```

```{r}
# Load data and select variables of interest
class_data <- read_csv('../data/background-clean.csv') %>% 
  select(stat.comf, stat.prof, courses)
head(class_data)
```
```{r}
# Summarize class dataset
summary(class_data)
```

```{r}
# Creating new columns corresponding to classes of interest
class_data <- class_data %>% 
  mutate(
    pstat_115 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 115'), 1, 0),
    pstat_160 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 160'), 1, 0),
    pstat_174 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 174'), 1, 0),
    pstat_175 = if_else(str_detect(courses, 'PSTAT 175'), 1, 0),
    adv_prof = if_else(str_detect(stat.prof, 'adv'), 1, 0)) %>% 
  select(-(c(courses, stat.prof)))
head(class_data)
```
```{r}
# Summarize class data
class_totals <- class_data %>% summarize(across(c(pstat_115, pstat_160,
                                                pstat_174, pstat_175), sum)) %>% 
                pivot_longer(cols=everything(),
                             names_to = 'course',
                             values_to = 'total')
  
# Plot class totals
class_barplot <- class_totals %>% ggplot(aes(x=course, y=total)) +
  geom_col(fill = '#005A87') +
  labs(title = 'Students Per Upper Division PSTAT Courses',
       x = 'Course',
       y = 'Total Students') +
  theme_light()
class_barplot
```
From this plot, we can see that over half of the students who provided their survey data have taken one or both PSTAT 160 courses (34 students). Less than half of these students took PSTAT 174 (12 students), and less than a quarter of students took PSTAT 115 (7 students) and PSTAT 175 (6 students) respectively. 

```{r}
# Summarize Student Comfort
comfort_barplot <- class_data %>% ggplot(aes(x = stat.comf)) + 
  geom_bar(fill = ('#2E6F40')) +
  labs(title = 'Student Statistics Comfort Count',
       x = 'Comfort',
       y = 'Total')
comfort_barplot
```
```{r}
# Get totals
comfort_totals <- class_data %>% count(stat.comf)
comfort_totals
```

From this plot and the comfort totals, we can see that over half the students who provided their survey data reported they have 4/5 comfortability with statistics. Over a quarter of the students reported a comfortability of 5/5, while 9 students reported a comfortability of 3/5.

## Building Model - Predicting Comfortability
```{r}
set.seed(2026)
# Split data
comfort_split <- initial_split(class_data, prop = 0.80, strata = stat.comf)
comfort_train <- training(comfort_split)
comfort_test <- testing(comfort_split)

# Check counts
nrow(comfort_train)
nrow(comfort_test)

```
39 observations in the training set, 12 in the testing set!

```{r}
# Create recipe
comfort_recipe <- recipe(stat.comf ~ pstat_115 + pstat_160 + 
                                   pstat_174 + pstat_175, 
                         data = comfort_train) 

# Model
comfort_model <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

# Workflow
comfort_wflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(comfort_model) %>%
  add_recipe(comfort_recipe)

# Fit and extract metrics
comfort_fit <- fit(comfort_wflow, comfort_train)

comfort_fit %>% 
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>% 
  tidy()
```

```{r}
# Evaluate RMSE and R-Squared
comfort_fit %>%
  predict(new_data = comfort_train) %>%
  bind_cols(comfort_train) %>%
  metrics(truth = stat.comf, estimate = .pred)
```

From these metrics, we can see that our model didn't do a very good job at predicting student comfortability with statistics. The RMSE is is about 0.769. This value is pretty high, which means that the model's predicted values were far from the actual values. The R-squared value is also low, about 0.18. This means that only 18% of the variance in student comfortability can be explained by our independent variables (our classes of interest). 

## Building Model - Predicting Proficiency
```{r}
# Split data
proficiency_split <- initial_split(class_data, prop = 0.80, strata = adv_prof)
proficiency_train <- training(proficiency_split)
proficiency_test <- testing(proficiency_split)
proficiency_folds <- vfold_cv(proficiency_train, v = 5, strata = adv_prof)

# Check counts
nrow(proficiency_train)
nrow(proficiency_test)
```

```{r}
# Create recipe
proficiency_recipe <- recipe(adv_prof ~ pstat_115 + pstat_160 + 
                                   pstat_174 + pstat_175, 
                         data = proficiency_train) 

# Model
proficiency_model <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm") %>%
  set_mode("regression")

# Workflow
proficiency_wflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(proficiency_model) %>%
  add_recipe(proficiency_recipe)

# Fit and extract metrics
proficiency_fit <- fit(proficiency_wflow, proficiency_train)

proficiency_fit %>% 
  extract_fit_parsnip() %>% 
  tidy()
```

```{r}
# Evaluate RMSE and R-Squared
proficiency_fit %>%
  predict(new_data = proficiency_train) %>%
  bind_cols(proficiency_train) %>%
  metrics(truth = adv_prof, estimate = .pred)
```
